items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #110: One Size Does Not Fit All
items.description:
In this reflective episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA presents her first solo podcast for September and builds it around a single argument: one size does not fit all. Thanking listeners who have written in, she makes the case that no template can meet every situation, because every person with a disability has a unique requirement and a unique set of needs, a mistake she admits making herself at times, and one she calls a lack of respect. It applies, she says, whether you are a phone rep, an agent, a teacher, a government department, or any other type of entity.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #109: Ask Advocate Donna
items.description:
In this practical episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA presents her September Ask Advocate Donna feature, opening with a favourite quotation, speak in such a way that others love to listen to you, listen in such a way that others love to speak to you, before turning to her recurring word game. She contrasts two pairs of advocacy words: commitment versus compliance, where committing is proactive and complying is merely following the leader, and afterthought versus forethought, illustrated with website developers who bolt on accessibility features at the end and managers who only remember employees with disabilities once the plan is already written.

The post Remarkable World Commentary Episode #109: Ask Advocate Donna appeared first on Donna J. Jodhan World-Renowned Blind Advocate.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #108: Interview with Peggy Chong, The Blind History Lady
items.description:
In this absorbing episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA speaks with Peggy Chong, The Blind History Lady, about how a 1979 job clearing out the files of a closing Minnesota home for the blind turned into a lifetime of recovering the lives of blind Americans. Peggy describes finding a board member's letter mentioning "our blind congressman," tracing it to Thomas David Schall, and calling him her first blind ancestor. She explains why she prefers storyteller to historian or archivist, and why she insists on telling the ordinary and the unflattering lives alongside the celebrated ones, because blind people are a cross section of society, crooks and murderers included.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #107: Interview with Ann Chiappetta, Author, Poet and President of Friends in Art
items.description:
In this moving episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA speaks with author, poet and Friends in Art president Ann Chiappetta about a life rebuilt three times over. Ann describes being diagnosed with retinitis pigmentosa in 1993 at 28, while expecting her first child, losing her job, her acrylic furniture design career, and for a while her sense of herself, and the "angels" who pulled her back: her ophthalmologist, her rehab counselor, and eventually writing itself, which she calls a catharsis for everything she could not say about going blind. She talks about the ten years she spent delivering the Building Bridges disability awareness program to children in kindergarten through second grade, and the payoff of overhearing a child in a supermarket teach their own parent not to touch a guide dog.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #106: Interview with Steve Barclay, Founder and President, Canadian Assistive Technology, and Co-Host, AT Banter Podcast
items.description: In this candid and unexpectedly personal episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA sits down with Steve Barclay, founder of Canadian Assistive Technology and co-host of the AT Banter Podcast, for a career-length walk through Canadian assistive technology. Steve begins in November 1990 as Aroga Technologies' very first employee, a bench technician repairing 40-pound CRT video magnifiers, Optacons, VersaBrailles and Prentke Romich Minspeak devices, and traces his climb to VP of Sales and Marketing and eventually part owner and chief operating officer. items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #105: Interview with Stephen Theberge, Science-Fiction Author and Accessibility Tester
items.description:
In this warm, unhurried episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan, LLB, ACSP, MBA talks with Stephen Theberge, a totally blind writer, software builder, and former ADA compliance tester from Attleboro, Massachusetts, about a life spent at the front edge of access technology. He traces the arc from 14 years as a residential student at the Perkins School for the Blind, through a Rhode Island College double major in computer science and English literature that began as an act of stubborn defiance after an advisor told him to switch, to running his own screen-reader business from the late 1980s until the big companies and the shift to graphical interfaces made a one-man operation impossible. Along the way he remembers punch cards and a dispatcher, a Texas Instrument computer that looked like a breadbox, the Covox Speech Thing wired to his own screen reader, and a 1992 WJAR television spot he still keeps.

items.title: Part 4: My Experience Trying To Take the Apex Program’s CompTIA Network+ Exam at a Pearson Vue Testing Center As A Blind Woman in Canada
items.description:
Here, Donna J. Jodhan returns to a Pearson Vue testing centre for a second attempt at the CompTIA Network+ exam, eight months after an inaccessible first sitting ended before it could begin. Pearson approved every accommodation she asked for and its staff treated her with real kindness, yet she met the same barrier that stopped her in October 2025: exam diagrams carrying no validated descriptions, improvised aloud by a reader who had never seen them. Along the way she was steered away from the JAWS screen reader she asked about, had her testing agreements recited to her because nobody mentioned they were available online to read herself, was given one person to perform two separately approved roles, and finally received her results on a sheet of paper she could not read. She did not pass, and she is candid about the cruelty at the heart of that: when the process is inaccessible, you never find out what you actually knew.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #102: Interview with Aaron Di Blasi, Sr. PMP, Mind Vault Solutions, Ltd., Regarding Her Ongoing Attempt To Take The Apex Program’s CompTIA Network+ Exam at a Pearson Vue Testing Center As A Blind Woman in Canada
items.description:
In this candid and unusually raw episode of Remarkable World Commentary, Donna J. Jodhan hands the microphone to her friend, associate and longtime collaborator Aaron Di Blasi for what he calls a "reverse grilling", a date-by-date walk through her two-year attempt to sit the CompTIA Network+ exam as a blind candidate. Beginning with the $7,500 Apex Program scholarship awarded in November 2024, they trace a scholarship that turned out to be 21 typo-riddled Word documents with no learning platform and no human support; a first exam abandoned in October 2025 when the reader said "I don't know what to do here"; the articles Donna published and the scholarship Apex withdrew because of them, telling her "you've made us the enemy"; the CNIB stepping in twice; and a second exam in May 2026 where the diagrams were still undescribed, the reader and recorder were one person, and her printed results had to be read aloud to her by a friend in the parking lot.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #104: Ask Advocate Donna
items.description:
Here Donna Jodhan steps into what she calls her Ask Advocate Donna shoes for her second solo episode of August, presenting stories of advocacy and inviting listeners to send in their own. She opens with a quote she came across and likes: speak in such a way that others love to listen to you, and listen in such a way that others love to speak to you. Then she runs her favourite word game, offering two pairs of words that advocates meet constantly. Action or conversation: action means getting involved, getting your hands dirty and your feet wet, the hardcore end of advocacy, while conversation means sitting down to listen and discuss, which is more passive. Intention or execution is the opposite pairing: intention is being ready and willing to get something done, execution is having actually done it. Donna is careful to say there is nothing wrong with either side of either pair, and that it depends on the advocate and where they want to go.

items.title: Remarkable World Commentary Episode #103: Entity or Customer
items.description: Here Donna Jodhan opens the month of August with a solo commentary she frames as entity versus customer, and she puts her opinion on the table straight away. When a form is inaccessible and the customer agent tells a blind or vision-impaired customer to go and find someone else to help them, whose responsibility is that really? Donna argues it belongs to the company and its agent, not to the customer: the form comes from the company, it does not come from her, and it is up to the agent to find a solution rather than to send someone elsewhere. She recounts what happened a few months ago with ServiceOntario, where an agent told her she had to find someone to assist her and she refused, in the most courteous way she could, then phoned again and again until she reached genuinely helpful, supportive agents who helped her complete and submit the form to renew her company's business.
